awarded.label: SAME_AREA

candidates.title: AtomWallet._validateSignature: validUntil/validAfter are appended to the signature but not part of the signed hash (time-bound malleability)
candidates.description: The 77-byte signature format appends uint48 validUntil + uint48 validAfter as a suffix, parsed by _extractValidUntilAndValidAfterFromSignature and returned in validationData. But the signed message is keccak256(\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n32, userOpHash) — userOpHash excludes the signature field, so the validUntil/validAfter bytes are NOT covered by the ECDSA signature. A bundler/relayer can alter the appended time bounds of an owner-signed userOp (extend or shrink its validity window) without invalidating the signature, since only (r,s,v) over userOpHash is checked.

candidates.title: TrustSwapAndBridgeRouter: bridge fee quoted on minTrustOut but bridges the actual (larger) amountOut; deadline=block.timestamp
candidates.description: swapAndBridgeWithETH/ERC20 compute bridgeFee = metaERC20Hub.quoteTransferRemote(domain, recipient, minTrustOut) but then _bridgeTrust(amountOut, ...) bridges the actual swap output amountOut (>= minTrustOut) with value=bridgeFee. If the Metalayer transfer fee scales with the bridged amount, the fee is under-quoted whenever amountOut > minTrustOut, causing transferRemote to revert (griefing/failed bridge) or under-payment. Separately, exactInput uses deadline=block.timestamp (no real deadline protection; slippage relies solely on amountOutMinimum).

candidates.title: TrustBonding.getUnclaimedRewardsForEpoch mixes max emissions with utilization-adjusted claims
candidates.description: getUnclaimedRewardsForEpoch returns getEmissionsAtEpoch(epoch) (MAX, unadjusted) minus totalClaimedRewardsForEpoch[epoch] (which is incremented by personal-utilization-ADJUSTED userRewards). Since epoch emissions are first scaled by systemUtilizationRatio (_emissionsForEpoch) and user shares again by personalUtilizationRatio, the 'unclaimed' figure conflates max vs doubly-adjusted claimed amounts — over-reporting unclaimed (the utilization-reduced portion is counted as reclaimable), which can over-recycle emissions if that value drives a reclaim/mint path.

candidates.title: AtomWallet transferOwnership/pendingOwner use hardcoded storage slots (mismatch would brick 2-step transfer)
candidates.description: transferOwnership writes _pendingOwner via a hardcoded AtomWalletPendingOwnerStorageLocation slot; acceptOwnership reads pendingOwner() (inherited). If the hardcoded constant does not exactly equal OZ Ownable2Step's ERC-7201 slot, the written pending owner and the read pending owner diverge and ownership claiming breaks. Low-confidence (the comment asserts the constant equals the OZ slot).
